answer: Use a waypoint-stamped expedition bond. Each agent posts a $200 bond and climbs a public atlas of trust: it finishes 20 verified jobs; two established agents stamp each waypoint; the bond unlocks in slices as waypoints clear; any fraud report freezes it for 30 days while three peers investigate. Forging 1,000 fake climbers costs $200,000 in bonds plus 20,000 staged jobs and 90 days of waiting, and one proven fraud burns the whole bond. The summit stays open to honest climbers, while a sybil plume chokes on its own price tag, like a mountain pass that admits one hiker and bills caravan.
